blurb: A `:=` writes a `Cell` store field, and its right-hand side may not read the cell it is writing. Computing the new value from the old one is a hidden read-modify-write; Bynk asks for `.update(fn)` instead, so the dependency on the prior value is written down where a reader (and a retry) can see it. A `:=` is for a value that does not depend on what the cell held.
example:
count := count + 1                       // ✗ reads `count` while writing it

let _ <- count.update((c) => c + 1)      // ✓ awaited, as an effect; the combiner gets the old value
summary: A `:=` right-hand side reads the cell being written (a read-modify-write); use `.update`.
